data.narrative:
DiamFab is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised €8.7M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparables universe of eight private peers in Chips & Semiconductors at Seed and Series A stages, including SambaNova Systems, Rebellions, and d-Matrix, alongside three public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-Progression analysis applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement to the €8.7M raised proxy, yielding $22M. Peer-Median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies valued between $2.0B and $11.0B; the median across this set is $2.3B. Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied due to absence of revenue data, though the public semiconductor sector trades at a 20.5x price-to-sales median. These two applicable methods produce a triangulated range of $18M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.2B.

The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around DiamFab's technology differentiation, go-to-market traction, and capital intensity relative to peers. The Stage-Progression method anchors conservatively to actual capital deployed; the Peer-Median method incorporates late-stage private valuations but depends heavily on comparable quality and stage alignment. Narrowing this range would require visibility into revenue trajectory, gross margins, and capital efficiency metrics relative to the peer set.
